# SOOS — Resource Governance Protocol (RGP)
# draft-sato-soos-rgp-00
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/rgp/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 13 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

The Resource Governance Protocol (RGP) is the SOOS governance layer
that enables a governed AI agent to discover what resources can do,
at what trust level they have been attested, and whether they are
currently available — before any task assignment is made in an AEP
session. RGP is NOT a booking or transaction protocol: discovery and
declaration are read-only operations. RGP is NOT a replacement for
ACD: ACD is the agent's compliance disclosure to a resource; RGP is
the resource's capability and governance declaration to the agent.

Version -00 is the initial submission. It defines: two-stage
discovery (Stage 1 well-known URI fingerprint, Stage 2 full
governance envelope), eight capability classes (CAP-COMP through
CAP-EXP), four trust levels (TRUST-0 through TRUST-3), the
session-scoped Resource Map Sovereign Object, the three-condition
autonomous fallback test (DEC-RGP-08), RGP-Model (AI model
capability declaration), and RGP-Physical (digital twin bindings).

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without RGP, a governed AI agent operating under a Mandate JWT
faces a resource landscape it cannot reason about under governance
constraints:

- Existing digital twin standards (AAS v3.0, W3C WoT, OPC UA,
  DTDL v3) describe what a resource can do but carry no trust
  attestation, no compliance declarations, no cost model, and no
  mandate-scope compatibility signal.

- AI model capability registries describe intrinsic model
  capabilities but provide no mandate-scoped capability set and no
  session-scoped assignment tracking.

- Without a normative fallback rule, an agent whose primary resource
  becomes unavailable has no governed basis for choosing a fallback —
  it either stops (blocking the session) or substitutes autonomously
  (potentially violating trust level, capability class, or budget
  constraints without principal awareness).

The consequence of absence: an agent that assigns tasks to resources
without governance envelope validation may: (1) select a resource
outside its mandate scope; (2) assign sensitive tasks to a lower-
trust resource than the principal requires; (3) exceed its mandate
budget through uncontrolled fallback chains; (4) produce no audit
record of why a resource was selected.

The analogy: in financial markets, a counterparty must declare its
regulatory status and eligible instrument classes before a trading
relationship is established. No trading desk accepts self-declaration
alone — independent attestation is required. RGP applies the same
principle to AI agent resource assignment.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

Resource: Any entity — physical device, digital service, AI model
instance, or human-in-the-loop node — that can receive task
assignments from a governed AI agent.

Capability Class: A standardized taxonomy label categorizing the
type of work a resource performs. Eight registered classes: CAP-COMP
(computational), CAP-STOR (storage), CAP-NET (network/API),
CAP-FAB (fabrication), CAP-COMM (communications), CAP-TXN
(transaction), CAP-HUMAN (human-in-the-loop), CAP-EXP
(experiential). A resource declares exactly one primary class.

Capability Fingerprint: The Stage 1 response from
/.well-known/soos-rgp. Minimum required fields: resource_id,
capability_class, trust_level, availability_status, valid_until.

Full Declaration: The Stage 2 governance envelope retrieved from
full_declaration_uri. Covers all nine governance dimensions:
capability class, operational constraints, temporal commitment,
exclusivity model, compliance declarations, cost model, trust level,
current state, output DA-Type.

Trust Level: A four-value attestation scale. TRUST-0: kernel-
generated, no external attestation. TRUST-1: attested by a
registered attestation authority (co-signature on Stage 2 required).
TRUST-2: self-attested with KIA-registered keys. TRUST-3:
unattested, no signature verification.

Resource Map Sovereign Object (Resource Map SO): The session-scoped
Sovereign Object constructed by the GEC from Stage 1 and Stage 2
query results. KIA-signed at construction. Records all queried
resources, mandate compatibility status, and assignment decisions.
MUST NOT be shared across AEP sessions.

Three-Condition Autonomous Fallback Test (DEC-RGP-08): An agent
MAY autonomously activate a fallback resource only if ALL THREE
conditions pass: (1) fallback trust_level >= primary trust_level;
(2) fallback capability_class covers the sub-goal; (3) fallback
cost stays within MJWT Resource Envelope budget. Any failing
condition triggers HEM: HEM-HIGH-1 (trust), HEM-PRE-2 (class),
HEM-DS-1 (budget).

Availability Status: Current operational state of a resource:
AVAILABLE, AT_CAPACITY, UNAVAILABLE, or MAINTENANCE.

Staleness Bound: The valid_until timestamp in the Stage 1
fingerprint. GEC MUST NOT use a fingerprint past valid_until.
Default cache window: 10 minutes, maximum 15 minutes.

RGP-Model: Extension of RGP for AI model instances as governed
resources. Two-layer model: Layer 1 (intrinsic capability) and
Layer 2 (mandate-scoped capability, derived at session start by
GEC). Discovered via /.well-known/soos-rgp?resource_type=MODEL.

RGP-Physical: Extension of RGP for physical resources declared
via digital twin standards. Normative field mappings for AAS v3.0,
W3C WoT 1.1, OPC UA, and DTDL v3 deferred post-Vienna (OQ-RGP-09).

Attestation Downgrade (ALE-027): Recorded when a resource's
attestation verification fails and its effective trust_level is
downgraded. Prevents silent trust level inflation.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

Well-Known URI (RFC 8615): Stage 1 fingerprint discovery uses the
/.well-known/soos-rgp pattern established by RFC 8615. Consistent
with the ACD pattern (/.well-known/soos-acd).

JWS/JWT (RFC 7519): Stage 2 full declarations for TRUST-1 resources
carry attestation authority JWS signatures. TRUST-2 resources carry
KIA self-signatures using the same JWS conventions.

TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446): All RGP discovery operations MUST use TLS 1.3
minimum. HTTP access to /.well-known/soos-rgp MUST be rejected.

Asset Administration Shell (AAS) v3.0: RGP-Physical Section 12.1
provides a governance overlay for AAS Submodel structures. Normative
field mappings deferred post-Vienna (OQ-RGP-09, Vienna engagement
with Qin Wu NMOP WG on ITU-T Y.3090 binding).

W3C WoT Thing Description 1.1: RGP-Physical Section 12.2 provides
a governance overlay via @context extension. Normative schema
deferred post-Vienna.

EU AI Act Article 13 (Transparency): The Resource Map SO and
GAR ALEs (ALE-022 through ALE-029) provide the machine-readable
assignment decision record that supports Article 13 compliance for
high-risk AI systems.

GDPR Article 25 (Data protection by design): Stage 2
compliance_declarations enable the GEC to verify data_protection_
framework compatibility before any data-handling task assignment.

Activity Travel Protocol (ATP) Layer 2: ATP Capability Declarations
(Layer 2 S3) are the application-layer expression of CAP-EXP
resource offerings. RGP Stage 1/Stage 2 is the governance discovery
layer that precedes the ATP booking workflow. Per DEC-RGP-11, the
normative ATP-RGP binding lives in a separate ATP-layer domain
profile document [ATP-RGP-PROFILE], not in this draft.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
- SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-02) — Resource Map SO is a Sovereign
  Object instance; output_da_type uses the SO Type Registry
- KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — GEC signing of Resource Map SO;
  TRUST-2 self-signature verification; TRUST-1 attestation authority
  key resolution
- MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02) — Resource Envelope (budget,
  capability class scope, can_decompose) bounds Resource Map SO
  construction
- AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — Resource Map SO is AEP session
  artifact; fallback pre-declaration references AEP EOD schema
- IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) — agent MUST NOT declare intent
  for a resource before RGP confirms mandate compatibility
- GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — ALE-022 through ALE-029 defined
  here are registered in the GAR ALE Type Registry
- HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-05) — DEC-RGP-08 fallback conditions
  trigger HEM-HIGH-1, HEM-PRE-2, or HEM-DS-1
- CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — CAP profile governs TRUST-3
  assignment prohibition by capability class; mandate-scope
  validation at assignment uses CAP profile
- KEE-1 (draft-sato-soos-kee-00) — GEC integrity properties P2
  (FROST signing) and P5 (Manifest hash-lock) underpin Resource
  Map SO signing integrity

The following drafts depend on this draft:
- GRP (draft-sato-soos-grp-00) — adopts DEC-RGP-08 verbatim as
  the normative FALLBACK action class boundary rule

Vienna engagement (IETF 126, July 18-24, 2026):
- Qin Wu (NMOP WG): OPC UA binding and ITU-T Y.3090 alignment for
  RGP-Physical (OQ-RGP-09)
- WIMSE WG: RGP as resource-side complement to WIMSE agent identity
  architecture

Post-Vienna work:
- OQ-RGP-01: Stage 1 minimum schema completeness
- OQ-RGP-04/05: Probabilistic model capability and drift signaling
- OQ-RGP-07: Reasoning Class registry (10 initial classes)
- OQ-RGP-09: Normative digital twin field mappings (AAS, WoT,
  OPC UA, DTDL)
- OQ-RGP-10: DNS-SD extension profile for local deployments
- OQ-RGP-12: Attestation authority multi-signing for high-stakes
  capability classes

Companion drafts at Vienna:
